zh: 交给我吧，我这就去办。
en: Leave it with me. I'm {on} it.
note: I'm on it means I have started dealing with it right now. It is a quick, confident reply to a request.

zh: 别担心这次故障，情况我都掌握了，正在处理。
en: Don't worry about the outage. I'm {across} it.
note: In New Zealand and Australia, I'm across it means I know all about it and I'm handling it.

zh: Mere了解新的休假政策吗？
en: Is Mere {across|on top of|up to speed on|aware of} the new leave policy?
note: Be across something is New Zealand and Australian English for knowing the details of it well.

zh: 我午饭后再回复你。
en: I'll get {back} to you after lunch.
note: Get back to someone means reply to them later, usually after you have checked something.

zh: 这个我们下周再回头讨论吧？
en: Can we {circle back|come back|get back} to this next week?
note: Circle back means return to a topic later. It is common office language, like coming back around in a circle.

zh: 想跟进一下我周一发的那封邮件。
en: Just {following up|checking in} on my email from Monday.
note: Follow up on something means check on it again after the first contact. It often starts a polite reminder email.

zh: 我会把你加进这个邮件往来里。
en: I'll {loop|copy|cc} you {in} on the email thread.
note: Loop someone in means add them so they get the information too. In means inside the group that knows.

zh: 一定要随时让Ben了解最新情况。
en: Make sure Ben's kept {in the loop|up to date|up to speed|informed}.
note: In the loop means part of the group that gets the latest news. Out of the loop means not told.

zh: Sarah休假期间，谁来接手她的工作？
en: Who's going to {take over} from Sarah while she's on leave?
note: Take over from someone means do their job after them. Over shows the work moves to a new person.

zh: 周五你能替我顶一下吗？我要去看牙医。
en: Can you {cover for|fill in for|stand in for} me on Friday? I've got a dentist appointment.
note: Cover for someone means do their work while they are away. For means in place of them.

zh: 最后一天我得把钥匙和电脑交出去。
en: I need to {hand over|hand back|hand in|give back|return} my keys and laptop on my last day.
note: Hand over means give something to the person who will be responsible for it. Over shows it moves to them.

zh: 财务批准买新电脑了吗？
en: Has finance {signed off on|approved|okayed} the new laptops yet?
note: Sign off on something means officially approve it. Off shows the decision is finished.

zh: 客户对价格提出了异议。
en: The client {pushed back on|objected to|questioned} the price.
note: Push back on something means disagree with it or resist it. Back shows you push in the opposite direction.

zh: 我们得把截止日期往后推一周。
en: We'll have to {push|move} the deadline {out|back} by a week.
note: Push a deadline out or back means make it later. Out shows it moves further into the future.

zh: 我们能把会议提前到周二吗？
en: Can we {bring|move} the meeting {forward} to Tuesday?
note: Bring a meeting forward means make it earlier. Americans often say move it up. Push it back means later.

zh: 发出去之前，我先让Sarah过目一下。
en: I'll {run} it {past|by} Sarah before we send it.
note: Run something past someone means show it to them quickly to get their opinion or OK.

zh: Tom今天请病假了。
en: Tom's {off|out} sick today.
note: Off sick means away from work because you are ill. Americans often say out sick.

zh: 我明天休息，有事找Mere。
en: I'm {off} tomorrow, so ask Mere if you need anything.
note: I'm off means I'm not working that day. Off means away from work.

zh: 她这个月底前都在休假。
en: She's {on} leave until the end of the month.
note: On leave means officially away from work, for a holiday or another reason. We say on leave, on holiday.

zh: 你休假什么时候回来？
en: When are you {back} from leave?
note: Back from leave means returning to work after time off. Back shows you return to where you were.

zh: 这个周末我值班待命，所以不能走远。
en: I'm {on call} this weekend, so I can't go far.
note: On call means ready to be called and start work if something breaks, even outside normal hours.

zh: 我周一前都不在办公室。
en: I'm {out of|away from} the office until Monday.
note: Out of the office means not at work. It is the usual phrase for automatic email replies.

zh: 你这周回办公室上班吗？
en: Are you {back in} the office this week?
note: Back in the office means working at the office again after time away or working from home.

zh: 全员大会需要有人做展示，你愿意试试吗？
en: We need someone to present at the all-hands. Are you {up for|keen on|game for} it?
note: Up for it means willing and ready to try. It is a friendly way to invite someone to do something.

zh: 如果你们要做云迁移，我很想参与进来。
en: If you're doing the cloud migration, I'd love to be {in on|part of|involved in} it.
note: Be in on something means be one of the people involved in it. In shows you are inside the group.

zh: 你现在在忙什么？有空问你个问题吗？
en: What are you {up to|working on|doing} at the moment? Got time for a quick question?
note: What are you up to asks what someone is doing. It is casual and very common at work and with friends.

zh: 这周我的工单有点积压了。
en: I'm a bit {behind on|behind with} my tickets this week.
note: Behind on something means you have not done as much as you should have by now.

zh: 她总能把邮件处理得井井有条。
en: She's always {on top of} her emails.
note: On top of something means in control of it, with nothing left undone. The opposite is behind on.

zh: 难得一次，我们进度提前了。
en: We're {ahead of} schedule for once.
note: Ahead of schedule means earlier than planned. Behind schedule means later than planned.

zh: 我现在忙得不可开交。
en: I'm completely {snowed under|swamped|flat out} at the moment.
note: Snowed under means you have so much work it feels like you are buried in snow.

zh: 今天我要早点下班，是我儿子生日。
en: I'm going to {knock off|finish|head off|clock off|leave} early today. It's my son's birthday.
note: Knock off is a casual New Zealand way to say finish work for the day.

zh: 好了，我先走了，明天见。
en: Right, I'm {heading off|off|heading home|off home|going|leaving}. See you tomorrow.
note: Heading off means leaving now. Off shows you are going away from this place.

zh: 你能跟我说说会上都讲了什么吗？
en: Can you {fill} me {in} on what happened at the meeting?
note: Fill someone in means tell them the information they missed. You fill in the gaps in what they know.

zh: 我去找财务催一下那张发票。
en: I'll {chase up|follow up|chase} the invoice with accounts.
note: Chase something up means ask again about something that is late. It is very common in New Zealand offices.

zh: 你有空的时候把那个发给我吧。
en: Can you {send} that {over|through|across} when you get a chance?
note: Send something over means send it to me. Over shows it moves from you to me.

zh: 我会把你的反馈转达给团队。
en: I'll {pass} your feedback {on|along} to the team.
note: Pass something on means give it to the next person. On shows it keeps moving forward.

zh: 周五团队聚餐？算我一个！
en: Team lunch on Friday? Count me {in}!
note: Count me in means include me, I want to join. Count me out means I don't want to join.

zh: 这次就别算我了，我要赶截止日期。
en: Count me {out} this time. I've got a deadline.
note: Count me out means don't include me. Out is the opposite of in.

zh: 周五的班把我排上吧。
en: Put me {down} for the Friday shift.
note: Put someone down for something means write their name on the list for it.

zh: 我一上午都脱不开身。
en: I'm {tied up|busy} all morning.
note: Tied up means too busy to do anything else, as if you cannot move.

zh: 你能接下这个入职项目吗？
en: Could you {take on|pick up|look after|handle} the onboarding project?
note: Take on means accept a new job or responsibility. On shows you add it to your work.

zh: 我明天接着上次停下的地方继续做。
en: I'll {pick up|carry on|continue} where I left off tomorrow.
note: Pick up where you left off means continue from the point where you stopped.

zh: 我们面临着很紧的截止日期。
en: We're {up against|facing|working to} a tight deadline.
note: Up against means facing a difficult problem or opponent. It shows something is working against you.

zh: 假期过后，工作又忙起来了。
en: Work's {picking up|getting busier} again after the holidays.
note: Pick up here means increase or get busier. Up shows more activity.

zh: 我明天会晚点到办公室，要去看医生。
en: I'll be {in} a bit late tomorrow. I've got a doctor's appointment.
note: Be in means be at work or in the office. Be in late means arrive at work late.

zh: 开会的时候你能支持我一下吗？
en: Can you {back} me {up} in the meeting?
note: Back someone up means support them, for example by agreeing with what they say.

zh: 大家都认同新流程吗？
en: Is everyone {on board} with the new process?
note: On board means agreeing with a plan and ready to help, like being on the same ship.

zh: 我们需要把答应过的事落实到底。
en: We need to {follow through} on what we promised.
note: Follow through means finish what you said you would do. Through shows you go all the way to the end.

zh: 她这周不在，下周一回来。
en: She's {away} this week. She's back on Monday.
note: Away means not here, often travelling or on holiday. Back means returned.

zh: 我现在要去客户办公室了。
en: I'm {off} to the client's office now.
note: I'm off to somewhere means I'm leaving now to go there. Off shows you are departing.
